hero.tagline: Where golden light meets the infinite dark

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Chandra's quiet dominion
moon.intro: Ptolemy believed the Moon's influence caused tides, madness, and the cycles of life. While science has explained the tides, the Moon still governs the menstrual cycle, the migration of birds, and the spawning of coral — life itself dances to the Moon's rhythm.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The ego: a wave believing itself alone
philosophy.intro: Nietzsche warned that 'whoever fights monsters should see to it that in the process he does not become a monster.' The ego, in its quest to prove its strength, often becomes the very thing it opposes.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: The soul that cannot be slain
gita.intro: In Chapter 11, Krishna reveals his Vishvarupa — the Universal Form — containing all worlds, all beings, all time. Arjuna sees the entirety of existence in one being and trembles. The infinite is not abstract; it is terrifyingly real.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva plays the damaru of creation
shiva.intro: Shiva sits in meditation on Mount Kailash, the axis mundi, the center of the world. His stillness is not inactivity — it is the stillness of a mind that has transcended all duality, all desire, all fear.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Beauty: the impermanent made eternal
art.intro: The flute is the oldest instrument — a hollow reed that sings when breath passes through it. It teaches that music is not made but revealed, not created but discovered in the space between silence and sound.
